Rules: real_exam/TEACHING_STYLE_GUIDE.md R1-R35 (no 'which way is better' verdict) + NITZAN_RHYTHM_DELIVERY.md P1-P13. Calm preset on the question reading and plain calculations.

slides.say: A printer cartridge has used fifty-seven point five percent of its ink. What fraction of the ink remains?
So they ask what's left, and the choices are fractions, not percents. We'll solve it in two different ways, the math way, and then with an insight from the choices.
Let's start with the math way. The whole cartridge is a hundred percent. Fifty-seven point five percent was used. So a hundred minus fifty-seven point five, forty-two point five percent is left.

slides: A lot of students turn the fifty-seven point five itself into a fraction. But that's the ink that was used. We want what's left.

slides.say: Now we turn the percent into a fraction. We write it over a hundred, forty-two point five over a hundred.
at: forty-two point five over a hundred

slides.say: A decimal point inside a fraction isn't nice. So we multiply the top and the bottom by two. Forty-two point five times two is eighty-five. A hundred times two is two hundred.
Now we reduce. Eighty-five and two hundred both divide by five. Eighty-five divided by five is seventeen. Two hundred divided by five is forty.
at: Eighty-five divided by five is seventeen
Two hundred divided by five is forty

slides.say: So it's seventeen over forty. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now the insight. These choices are not random. We start again from the givens. Fifty-seven point five percent was used, so forty-two point five percent is left.
Start with an easy fraction from our table. A twentieth is five percent.
Look at choice number three, seventeen over twenty. It has seventeen twentieths. So seventeen twentieths is seventeen times five, eighty-five percent. That's not forty-two point five, so it's out.

But look at choice number two, seventeen over forty. Its bottom is twice as big, so it's exactly half of seventeen over twenty. Half of eighty-five percent is forty-two point five percent. That's exactly what's left.
And choice number one, twenty-three over forty? Twenty-three is forty minus seventeen. So it's the rest of the cartridge, the fifty-seven point five percent that was used. That's the trap.
The exam often builds the choices like this, so a student who looks at them carefully gets there fast. Choice number two is our answer.
We can also start with one fortieth. It is half of one twentieth. Half of five percent is two point five percent.
at: Half of five percent is two point five

slides.say: Seventeen fortieths are seventeen times that amount. Seventeen times two is thirty-four. Seventeen times a half is eight point five. Thirty-four plus eight point five is forty-two point five percent.
at: Seventeen times a half is eight point five

slides.say: That is the ink left. Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
